company.name: Mason Stevens
company.description: Integrated wealth platform technology provider targeting HNW/UHNW clients via financial advisers. Offers portfolio administration, managed accounts, and outsourced CIO services.

revenue_streams.name: Platform Administration Fees
revenue_streams.notes: Basis-point fee on AUM; adjusted Feb 2025

revenue_streams.name: Outsourced CIO Services
revenue_streams.notes: Direct investment advisory for UHNW clients

cost_structure: Platform technology maintenance and ATHENA modernisation project
Custodial and settlement infrastructure (50+ partner network)
business_model.value_proposition: Adviser-driven, HNW-focused platform with broader asset class access (fixed income, international equities, FX, derivatives, unlisted) than mass-market platforms; more bespoke than large generic competitors.

strengths.detail: Niche positioning in a segment where fees and LTV are highest
Access to direct fixed income, FX, derivatives, international equities — rare for adviser platforms
Execution infrastructure larger players struggle to replicate quickly
Platform built around adviser workflow, not retail self-directed — sticky distribution
Adamantem Capital brings capital for M&A and accelerated growth; prior constraint was organic-only
Differentiated service layer competitors don't offer at platform level
Investment Trends recognition signals improving product

weaknesses.detail: Significantly less scale means higher unit cost per client and less bargaining power
Lowest among 5 major platforms benchmarked; real capability gaps exist
Thin operational coverage; adviser support response times at risk during growth
Not a household name; advisers default to Hub24/Netwealth unless actively sold to
Digital modernisation project signals prior platform was behind; migration risk
Entirely dependent on adviser intermediaries; vulnerable if RG146/fee-for-service reform reduces adviser numbers
ATHENA partnership suggests data/reporting was a weakness; institutional clients expect sophisticated analytics
Private ownership reduces transparency; harder to benchmark performance publicly

opportunities.detail: Peter Mermolas hire (ex-Morgan Stanley Family Office) signals this; underserved by current platforms
Adamantem backing enables bolt-on acquisitions (technology, distribution, AUM)
Larger advice practices forming; Mason Stevens' bespoke model suits consolidators vs generic platforms
HNW clients increasingly demand private equity, credit, real assets — Mason Stevens has the infrastructure others lack
Multi-currency/multi-asset platform is infrastructure for Asian/Pacific expansion
No Australian adviser platform has differentiated on AI yet — first mover window open
Regulatory trends toward direct SMSF management create channel-bypass opportunity
Adamantem is impact-focused PE; natural product extension for adviser-led ESG mandates

threats.detail: Both have 6x+ the AUM, more features, more advisers — network effects compound
Platform fees falling industry-wide; small players feel this proportionally more
Compliance costs growing; disproportionate impact on smaller platforms
Post-Hayne royal commission, Australia has significantly fewer financial advisers — smaller addressable market
Direct-to-consumer robo-advice, neobrokers eroding the adviser channel from below
PE ownership could lead to on-sell; disruption to adviser relationships
Competing for tech and investment talent with Big 4 banks, Macquarie, global fintechs

direct_competitors.name: Hub24
direct_competitors.differentiator: Market leader, broadest adviser adoption, technology investment

direct_competitors.name: Netwealth
direct_competitors.differentiator: Strongest technology reputation, direct client channel

direct_competitors.name: Praemium
direct_competitors.differentiator: SMA/managed account specialist, strong international presence

direct_competitors.name: BT Panorama
direct_competitors.differentiator: Westpac bank-backed, large existing client base

direct_competitors.name: Mason Stevens
direct_competitors.differentiator: Multi-asset breadth, HNW specialist, outsourced CIO

strategic_gaps: Weak brand presence vs scale competitors
Data infrastructure in transition (ATHENA not fully live)
No mobile-first experience for end clients
No automated tax-loss harvesting at scale
Limited ESG/impact product suite despite PE owner focus
No public performance track record (private company)
